transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-11 15:30 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Nguyen (Redwood AE), Ben Carter (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel (Moonlit CTO), Elena Garcia (ML Eng), Samir Khan (Infra Lead), Priya Rao (PM), Jordan (intern)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be brief): Discussed options to get Moonlit to first API call quickly, privacy requirements leaning towards VPC but open to hosted trial; action items centered on security artifacts and benchmark plan.

00:00:00 - Alice (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro from our side, I'm Alice, AE working with platform and self-serve. Ben is our SE and will walk through technical fit. Maya is on CS. Could each of you do quick intros?
00:00:18 - Raj (Moonlit CTO): Sure. I'm Raj, CTO. We build an in-app assistant for our content creation suite. Right now we're prototype-ing features, want to understand time-to-first-token and privacy.
00:00:30 - Elena (ML Eng): Elena, ML engineer, mainly concerned about latency and how we preserve context, tokenization differences, and the KV cache-ish behavior across requests.
00:00:45 - Samir (Infra): Samir, infra. I look after network and security. We have residency needs for EU data and want KMS integration.
00:00:54 - Priya (PM): Priya, PM here to triage success criteria.

00:01:05 - Ben (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda: 1) where you're at today, 2) TTFT/runway to first call and credits, 3) hosting options—hosted, dedicated, private/VPC—4) security checklist and 5) next steps. Sound good?
00:01:18 - Raj: Yup. We're on a deadline to have a working prototype within three weeks. Ideally, first API call tomorrow but realistically within the week. We have a moderate volume expectation at first, maybe 10-20 requests per second later.

00:01:40 - Alice: Okay, so short runway. Our usual PLG path is: we give free credits, you sign up, hit the hosted API, get to first token in minutes using our SDKs. If that meets latency/privacy, you stay hosted. If not, we can move to Dedicated or Private.
00:02:00 - Samir: Quick question — how much of our data would leave our VPC if we use hosted? We need to make sure customer PII doesn't leak.
00:02:10 - Ben: On hosted, requests go to Redwood's hosted control plane, but content isn't used for training and is encrypted at rest. We also have data retention controls and audit logs. We can provide our SOC2 summary and encryption details. For strong compliance you can use Dedicated or Private; Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane and optional on-prem.
00:02:35 - Elena: Is there a middle ground where we keep keys locally? We want to own the KMS.
00:02:42 - Ben: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS in some configurations; Private/VPC supports full KMS with HSM integrations. There's also token-level encryption options. I'll add a note — need to check exact KMS providers we support for EU regions.

00:03:05 - Priya: For success metrics, we want median latency under 120ms and p99 under 500ms for short prompts (~64 tokens). Is that realistic on hosted?
00:03:18 - Ben: That depends on model and route. For smaller open models optimized for latency you'll see medians in that ballpark from hosted in the same region. p99 can be higher depending on burst and batching. Dedicated reduces variance with reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. We can run a quick benchmark using your prompt set to surface realistic numbers.
00:03:45 - Raj: OK. And how do we get started with the free credits?
00:03:50 - Alice: I'll provision credits for you today. The typical flow is: sign up, grab the API key, run our quickstart (curl / SDK) — we have a sample repo. Most teams see first token within 10–20 minutes if they already have the prompt id and basic env setup.
00:04:08 - Jordan (intern): Does the quickstart include streaming examples?
00:04:12 - Ben: Yes, streaming SDKs for Node/Python. We'll send a sample that shows streaming to the UI.

00:04:28 - Samir: Network-wise, do you support whitelist IPs for outbound? We prefer to do VPC peering or private endpoints rather than open egress.
00:04:35 - Ben: For hosted we support allow-listing origins and IPs, but if you require no public egress, Private deployment with managed VPC or on-prem is the path. Dedicated can also be set up in a customer's cloud account with some private connectivity.

00:04:56 - Elena: Any quirks with tokenization? We use a mixture of utf-8 and some special tokens for our annotation flow. Curious about model families and differences.
00:05:05 - Ben: Models vary, and tokenizers too. We'll map your prompts to recommended model variants; for low-latency you'll sacrifice some quality sometimes. We can run a quick regen test. Also note our runtime does KV cache and prefix caching; in streaming stateful flows cache behavior affects p99.

00:05:35 - Raj: We also need audit logs for compliance. Can you provide request-level logs and who accessed keys?
00:05:43 - Ben: We provide request traces, token-level cost breakdowns on the Console, and audit logs for API keys and role changes. For Private, you get full central logging in your account and can forward to Splunk. We'll share an audit log sample.

00:06:05 - Priya: How long does it usually take to spin up Dedicated for a pilot?
00:06:10 - Alice: Dedicated provisioning is typically a multi-week process if you want reserved capacity. For a short pilot we can do a scoped Dedicated-esque environment where we reserve a pool for you, but the fastest is hosted trial. Then if the pilot shows predictable need we'll move to Dedicated commitment.
00:06:30 - Raj: Budget is limited for now; we'd prefer hosted trial unless hosted doesn't meet latency/risk.

00:06:42 - Ben: Sounds practical. Let's talk TTFT: if you sign up today and we provision credits, median customer experience is — sign up, install SDK, run sample prompts; first token within 5–15 minutes typically. If you hit any environment hurdles we can pair-program the quickstart.

00:07:05 - Elena: For the benchmark, what data do you need from us?
00:07:09 - Ben: Ideally: 1) a 1k sample prompt set representative distribution (short/long), 2) expected concurrency targets (RPS), 3) region preference, 4) any constraints (no external connectivity). With that we can run token-level latency and cost estimates and run an actual runner against hosted or a dedicated test pool.

00:07:38 - Raj: We'll assemble that. One more: do you have a grace period for spike traffic? We might have sudden bursts from marketing campaigns.
00:07:47 - Alice: Yes; hosted has burst capacities, and you can configure autoscaling. Dedicated has burst options and reserved headroom. We can propose autoscale policies.

00:07:58 - Samir: If we start hosted and then go Private, how painful is migrating keys and model pins?
00:08:05 - Ben: We support model pinning and versioning. Migrating keys is mainly a config step; data residency and audit logs move with your account in Private. There are operational steps but it's designed to be relatively smooth. We'll share a migration runbook.

00:08:25 - Priya: Who are some peers using Redwood in regulated spaces? Any reference we can talk to?
00:08:31 - Alice: We can connect you with a healthcare customer that started hosted and moved to Dedicated; we'll check permission and share contacts.

00:08:42 - Raj: One blocker — we need SSO/SAML and RBAC before any pilot with real data. Is that supported on hosted?
00:08:50 - Ben: Hosted supports SSO for workspace logins and RBAC on the Console. For API-level SSO and stronger SAML integration with your IdP you might prefer Dedicated or Private. I'll list exact SAML providers we support.

00:09:10 - Jordan (intern): Do you have sample cost numbers for embeddings vs text generation?
00:09:15 - Maya (CSM): We'll send a cost spreadsheet template. For quickstart the free credits let you experiment without charges; we'll provide typical unit costs too.

00:09:30 - Ben: Quick aside on tooling: Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdown, per-model dashboards, and quick traces so you can see p50/p95/p99 by route and model. That helps tune batching and caching for cost/latency tradeoffs.

00:09:52 - Elena: About batching — we are very latency-sensitive; we avoid batching in the interactive path. Can Redwood let us disable batching per route?
00:10:00 - Ben: Yes, batching policies are configurable per-route. You can set max latency, batch sizes, and also have separate routes for interactive low-latency vs bulk gen.

00:10:16 - Raj: Any NDAs we need before sharing prompt data?
00:10:20 - Alice: We have an NDA template and can sign an MSA if you prefer. For initial quickstart we can work with redacted/sample prompts; if you're sharing customer PII we'll do an NDA/DP agreement.

00:10:35 - Priya: Great. Let's outline immediate next steps so everyone is clear.
00:10:41 - Alice: I'll summarize: 1) Alice to send SOC2 summary, security whitepaper, data retention and KMS notes by tomorrow (5/12). 2) We'll provision free credits and quickstart repo link today. 3) Ben will prepare a lightweight benchmark runner and instructions by Friday (5/15). 4) Moonlit to share 1k prompt sample and target RPS by 5/14. 5) Schedule a pilot scoping session (infra-focused) for week of 5/18.
00:11:10 - Raj: That works. Any concerns about timeline?
00:11:14 - Ben: If hosted works we can have a functional prototype in a few days. If you require Private we should start legal and security review in parallel since provisioning will take longer.

00:11:30 - Elena: Minor note: we use some custom tokens, so Ben, please include tokenizer mapping steps in the runner instructions.
00:11:38 - Ben: Will do.

00:11:45 - Samir: For KMS and HSM, what vendors do you integrate with?
00:11:49 - Ben: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and some HSMs in Private builds. I'll confirm specific HSM versions and document it.

00:11:58 - Priya: Sounds good. One last item — how do refunds/credits work if we hit quota?
00:12:04 - Maya: We manage credits centrally; we'll top you up for the pilot and notify you before they expire. If you need more we can expand.

00:12:12 - Alice: Anything else from Moonlit?
00:12:16 - Raj: No, I think we've covered it. Looking forward to the security packet and the credits.

00:12:23 - Alice: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the scoping call.

(Small crosstalk and hangups as people drop)

00:12:45 - End of recording

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mislabels and auto-caption errors; proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., specific HSM model numbers).

Appendix: shared links mentioned (to be sent): quickstart repo (redwood/quickstart-samples), SOC2 summary doc, security whitepaper, benchmark runner repo, cost spreadsheet template.
